simple.meaning: אַל (ʼal) is a Hebrew object word meaning “not.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Daniel 2:24. The surrounding context includes family line, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַל (H409) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אַל (ʼal) / H409 is traced through Daniel 2:24, Daniel 4:16, Daniel 5:10 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Therefore Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon. He went and said this to him: “Don’t destroy the wise men of Babylon. Bring me in before the king, and I will show to the king the interpretation.”

timeline.evidenceText: Therefore Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon. He went and said this to him: “Don’t destroy the wise men of Babylon. Bring me in before the king, and I will show to the king the interpretation.”
Let his heart be changed from man’s, and let an animal’s heart be given to him. Then let seven times pass over him.

The queen by reason of the words of the king and his lords came into the banquet house. The queen spoke and said, “O king, live forever; don’t let your thoughts trouble you, nor let your face be changed.

definitions.full: H409. al אַל adverb of prohibition, do not . . ., let not . . . , followed by imperfect ( = Biblical Hebrew I. אַל ; Zenjirli אל (Had 22. 23. 29 ) Cooke 160f. ; compare Pahlavi (Nö GGA, 1884, 1016 ); not ᵑ7 Syriac); — Dan 2:24 אַלֹתְּֿהוֺבֵד , 4:16 ; 5:10 .
